coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: P26
record.summary: A triangular landscaped wedge in the freeway-ramp interchange near 16th Street, 3rd Street and Owens Street, next to the UCSF Medical Center campus; real landscaped/grassed land per satellite imagery, delineated by this project's owner-directed real-gap-fragment method rather than a surveyed parcel boundary or a named park record. Name, operator and construction date not confirmed by any source found -- and this project's own 'P26' label for it does not match OCII's official current numbering (see open_questions).

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/grassed land per Esri satellite imagery and the street/already-tracked-polygon-bounded gap computation, not a surveyed footprint or named park record. Name and operator (likely SFMTA/Caltrans ramp landscaping or an OCII-era open-space installation, matching its P26 plan designation) not confirmed by any source found in this pass.
notes.digitized_from: Real-gap-fragment technique: bbox.difference(street buffer).difference(already-tracked polygons) near the UCSF Medical Center campus. The owner reviewed the numbered fragment map and picked fragment 49 as P26's real extent, then directed a further cut: the fragment forks into two thin parallel strips (~13-21m wide, running north alongside a building courtyard) above a wider single base (up to 46m wide) -- keep the base, drop both forks.

open_questions: OCII's own current public Mission Bay South open-space page (src-ocii-openspace-page) labels 'P26' as Mariposa Park -- a real, much larger (2.5-acre) named park with a playground at Mariposa and Owens streets, developed alongside UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital and reported to have opened in spring 2016 (src-potreroview-mariposa) -- not this record's small (~2,037 sqm) freeway-interchange landscaping wedge. This project's own 'P26' label for this wedge, per its digitization_method log, was instead assigned during this project's own numbered real-gap-fragment review, not sourced to any city document naming this specific wedge P26. This is a likely label mismatch, not resolved or corrected here since it would require a geometry-file change, which is out of scope for this dossier pass.

No construction date found for this wedge itself; it sits near UCSF Medical Center at Mission Bay, which opened February 1, 2015 (per this repo's own record ucsf_mission_bay_hospital), but no source ties this landscaping's own completion to that date.
Name and operator (this project's own digitization_method log guesses SFMTA/Caltrans ramp landscaping or an OCII-era open-space installation) not confirmed by any source found.
